candidate.answerReason: Noncollinear normals exclude parallel and coincident planes, so the planes intersect in a line. Perpendicularity is not forced.

methods.label: Exclude parallelism and coincidence
methods.explanation: If the normal vectors are not collinear, the two planes have different orientations and must intersect. Whether they are perpendicular also depends on whether the dot product is 0.
methods.levelReason: Uses the standard classification of plane positions and elective normal-vector criteria.

review.mathematicalCheck: Parallel or coincident planes have collinear normals. Noncollinear normals exclude both, so the planes intersect in a line, choice C. The additional statement is also valid: perpendicular planes have normals with zero dot product, which noncollinearity alone does not force.
